description: SAP Interview Coach. Every number this module reports - each dimension score, the overall score, the bands, the weak/strong thresholds and the study plan - is produced by deterministic Python from the values below. A language model is only ever asked for prose, and the prose arrives in its own fields. Editing this file changes the marking with no code change.

scoring.description: The explicit rubric. Concept coverage drives technical accuracy, completeness, business understanding and architecture; the shape of the answer drives clarity; known-wrong statements cost technical accuracy points only.

clarity.description: Clarity is measured from the shape of the answer, never from its vocabulary: a candidate who says the right things badly should lose clarity marks and keep their technical accuracy.

sap_mm.label: SAP MM
sap_mm.description: Materials management: master data, purchasing documents, release strategies, the document flow from requisition to payment, and inventory movements.

sap_ariba.label: SAP Ariba
sap_ariba.description: Sourcing, contracts, guided buying, supplier management and how each of them lands back in the ERP.

sap_s4hana.label: SAP S/4HANA
sap_s4hana.description: What changed from ECC, the simplification items that touch procurement, embedded analytics, Fiori and conversion approaches.

sap_business_network.label: SAP Business Network
sap_business_network.description: Trading partner onboarding, document exchange across the network, and the commercial and operational model behind it.

sap_integration.label: SAP Integration
sap_integration.description: IDocs, APIs, events, middleware, error handling and monitoring between SAP and everything else.

sap_architecture.label: SAP Architecture
sap_architecture.description: Landscape design, deployment options, extensibility, data residency and the trade-offs an architect has to argue for.

procurement.label: Procurement
procurement.description: Category management, sourcing strategy, negotiation, supplier performance and the numbers a buyer is measured on.

supply_chain.label: Supply chain
supply_chain.description: Demand planning, inventory policy, lead times, service levels and the working capital they cost.

sap_consulting.label: SAP consulting scenarios
sap_consulting.description: Requirements workshops, scope disputes, go-live pressure, stakeholder handling and the judgement calls a consultant is hired for.

selection.description: Which questions a session is built from. The selection is seeded, so the same request always produces the same interview - a demo can be repeated and a test can assert on it.

practice.label: Practice
practice.description: Untimed practice across the difficulty range. Feedback is shown after every answer.

timed.label: Timed interview
timed.description: A full interview with a per-question time limit. The clock is recorded and reported; it never changes a score.

technical.label: Technical interview
technical.description: Configuration, master data, document flow and troubleshooting depth. Technical accuracy carries the most weight.

architecture.label: Architecture interview
architecture.description: Landscape, integration patterns, deployment options and non-functional trade-offs. The architecture dimension is weighted heavily and every question in this mode carries architecture concepts.

behavioral.label: Behavioral interview
behavioral.description: Stakeholder handling, delivery pressure and consulting judgement. Clarity and business understanding carry the most weight.

rapid_fire.label: Rapid-fire questions
rapid_fire.description: Short definitional questions with a one-minute limit. A rapid-fire answer is not a short essay, so the clarity length band is narrower here.

performance.description: How the dashboard decides what is weak, what is strong and what to study next.

study_plan.description: The recommended study plan is derived from the recorded answers - the weakest topics and the concepts most often missed on them. Nothing here is generated by a model.
default_actions: Re-read your notes on {topic} and write a five-sentence definition from memory.
Answer three more {topic} questions in practice mode and compare each answer with the reference answer.
Explain {topic} out loud to somebody who does not work in SAP, then note which part you had to look up.

sap_mm: Walk the {topic} document flow end to end on paper: requisition, purchase order, goods receipt, invoice, payment - and name the document each step creates.
List the master data {topic} depends on and what breaks when each one is wrong.
sap_ariba: Sketch how {topic} moves between Ariba and the ERP, naming what is replicated in each direction.
Write down which part of {topic} is configured in Ariba and which part is configured in the ERP.
sap_s4hana: Note what changed in {topic} between ECC and S/4HANA, and why the change was made.
List the simplification items that touch {topic} and what each one asks a project to do.
sap_business_network: Describe how a trading partner is onboarded for {topic} and what each side has to agree first.
Write down which documents cross the network for {topic} and in which direction.
sap_integration: Draw the interface for {topic}: protocol, payload, error handling, monitoring and who is called when it fails.
Write down how {topic} behaves when the receiving system is unavailable.
sap_architecture: Sketch the landscape for {topic} and mark every point where data crosses a system boundary.
Write two paragraphs on the trade-off {topic} forces, and what you would need to know to decide it.
procurement: Write the business case for {topic} in five bullet points a category manager would recognise.
List the numbers a buyer would use to prove {topic} worked.
supply_chain: Work {topic} through with real numbers: demand, lead time, safety stock and the resulting order date.
Name the trade-off {topic} makes between service level and working capital.
sap_consulting: Rewrite your answer on {topic} using the situation, task, action, result structure.
Note one project where {topic} went badly and what you would do differently.

feedback.description: Size limits and wording for the deterministic feedback. A drafted answer that breaks one of these limits is repaired field by field and the repair is recorded, exactly as in modules 8 and 9.

templates.strength_clarity: The answer is well structured and easy to follow.
templates.strength_length: The answer is the right length for the question.
templates.strength_none: Nothing in this answer matched the marking scheme yet.
templates.improved_answer_intro: A complete answer to this question covers the following.
templates.coaching_note_pass: This answer would pass. Tighten the parts listed above and it would be a strong one.
templates.coaching_note_borderline: This answer is close. The missing concepts below are what separates it from a pass.
templates.coaching_note_fail: Work through the study topics below before answering this one again.
templates.coaching_note_non_answer: No answer was given, so nothing could be scored. Say what you do know, even partially - an interviewer can work with a partial answer and cannot work with silence.
templates.follow_up_default: Can you say more about the part of your answer you are least sure of?

reporting.disclaimer: This coach practises interview technique against a bundled, entirely fictional question bank. The scores come from the published rubric in this configuration file, not from a language model and not from any SAP certification scheme. Nothing here is an SAP qualification, and no answer has been reviewed by SAP.
reporting.ai_note: Scores, bands, concept matching and the study plan are calculated by deterministic Python. When an AI provider is active it may rewrite the feedback prose and the improved sample answer; those fields carry their own origin label and never change a score.
reporting.scoring_note: Concept matching is keyword based. A correct answer phrased in words the bank does not list will score lower than it deserves - the matched keyword is shown next to every concept so you can see exactly what was and was not credited.
